options: The mechanism a test uses to decide pass or fail
questions.explanation: An oracle decides whether output is acceptable. AI testing usually stacks several: exact, property, metamorphic, reference-based and human.

options: Every citation points to a retrieved document
Two paraphrases get the same label
questions.explanation: Properties are invariants every acceptable output satisfies. The first is exact, the third metamorphic and the fourth human review.

questions.prompt: Changing only the prompt text is a configuration change and does not need a regression eval.
questions.explanation: False. Prompt and model changes alter behaviour like code releases; treating them as configuration is a listed mistake.

questions.prompt: Eval results changed overnight with no commit. The app calls a floating model alias. What is the likely cause and fix?
options: The provider updated the model behind the alias; pin a specific model version and treat upgrades as releases
questions.explanation: Using a floating alias means behaviour changes without your code changing. Pin versions so changes are deliberate and tested.

questions.prompt: Which layer best catches a bug where the JSON parser crashes on an empty tool result?
options: Unit tests of the deterministic code with a fake model client
questions.explanation: Parsers, guards and tool code are deterministic and cheap to unit-test with fakes. Forgetting that layer is a listed mistake.

questions.prompt: Which are metamorphic relations you could test for a sentiment classifier? Select all that apply.
options: Adding irrelevant text does not change the sentiment
Swapping a person's name does not change the score beyond a tolerance
questions.explanation: Metamorphic oracles compare outputs across related inputs, so they work without a known expected value. JSON validity is a contract/property check.

questions.prompt: Your eval dataset has 400 English cases about billing and none about cancellations, other languages, or very long inputs. What concept reveals this gap?
options: Input-space coverage: a matrix of intents, languages, lengths, adversarial patterns and segments with empty cells
questions.explanation: Code coverage says little about model behaviour. Input-space coverage shows which important cells have no examples.

questions.prompt: A test fails in 3 of 10 nightly runs. The team marks it flaky and skips it. What is the better practice?
options: Treat the pass rate as the signal: run k samples, record the rate per case, gate on thresholds, and investigate the failing outputs
questions.explanation: For AI, failures often appear as a lower pass rate rather than a reproducible crash. Measuring rates is the oracle; skipping hides real defects.

questions.prompt: Where should production failures end up in a mature AI testing strategy?
options: As new cases (with tags) in the eval dataset, so the regression suite learns from real failures
questions.explanation: A production feedback loop grows the dataset with real failures; without it the dataset never learns.

coding.title: Metamorphic invariance check
coding.prompt:
Write `invariance_failures(classify, cases)` where `classify(text)` returns a label and `cases` is a list of `(case_id, original, variants)` tuples. A case fails if any variant gets a different label from the original. Return the list of failing case ids in order.

This is how you test that paraphrases ('My card was stolen' vs 'Someone stole my card') get the same label without knowing the right label in advance.
coding.explanation: A metamorphic oracle checks a relationship between outputs rather than an expected value, which is ideal when many outputs are acceptable or no gold label exists.
hints: Compare every variant's label with it.
Collect the ids of cases where any differ.

tests.name: Finds a paraphrase inconsistency
tests.code:
def clf(t):
    return 'fraud' if 'stolen' in t else 'general'
cases=[('c1','My card was stolen',['Someone stole my card']),('c2','My card was stolen',['my card was STOLEN'.lower()])]
assert invariance_failures(clf,cases)==['c1'], invariance_failures(clf,cases)

coding.title: Pass rate per case over k runs
coding.prompt: Write `flaky_report(run_results, min_rate)` where `run_results` maps a case id to a list of booleans (one per run). Return a dict with `rates` (case id -> rate rounded to 2 decimals), `failing` (sorted ids whose rate is below `min_rate`) and `overall` (mean of all individual runs, rounded to 2 decimals).
coding.explanation: Per-case rates turn 'flaky' into a measurement. Gating on a minimum rate per case, plus an overall number, replaces exact-string assertions and retry-until-green.
hints: Flatten all runs for the overall rate.
